headline: Maui County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee
meeting.summary: The committee recommended board nominees and four claim settlements and will return March 30 at 9 a.m.
meeting.recap: A nominee to the Cultural Resources Commission said he served a four-year term on it years ago.[[0:12:04]] The chair deferred his nomination because it is already on Friday's full Council agenda to meet a deadline.[[0:28:21]] Members voted nine to zero to remove the reappointment wording from his resolution.[[0:41:53]] A county attorney said three of the claims before the committee involved flooding.[[1:37:37]] The Water Department said it has started checking the condition of the whole water system.[[1:44:13]] A county attorney said the other side in a lawsuit agreed to drop its appeal in exchange for a tentative settlement.[[1:55:11]] He asked to discuss it in executive session (a closed-door discussion).[[1:55:51]] The committee will return on March 30 at 9 a.m. to take up three remaining items.[[2:12:47]]
meeting.next: Three remaining agenda items will be taken up on the 30th at 9 a.m. A council member said she would try to file a change for Friday so the nominee clearly fills the cultural practitioner seat.

moments.q: "half the battle in anything is showing up"
"I've never been on a county board or commission before."

Request for executive session on lawsuit settlement

boards.name: Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee

issues.oneLine: The County is settling claims for damage to homes from water main breaks.
issues.why: A council member said the damage was substantial and was not the residents' doing.
issues.next: The Water Department said a condition assessment of the whole water system will show where repairs or replacement are needed.
issues.brief: One claim, for $13,593.87, involved a water main break at a Kīhei property.[[#1]] A nominee said a meeting that evening would discuss five wells the County wants to put in for Lahaina.[[#2]] The Water Department said getting a new vehicle to replace a totaled truck could take two to three years.[[#3]] Members were told the County is self-insured, so it pays these claims itself.[[#4]]
